subject: Post-demo: crypto, residency & logging clarifications
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samar Gupta <samar.gupta@finpay.com>, Elena Korsakov <ekorsakov@finpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: crypto, residency & logging clarifications

Hi Samar / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick follow-up while the items are fresh. I captured the items we promised to clarify on encryption, logging, and residency:

- Data residency: you asked about pinning customer data to US-east only for production. Confirming Redwood supports region routing + tenant pinning — we can talk SLA/backup geography tradeoffs.
- In-transit encryption: we use TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS option for Dedicated/Private; happy to provide handshake details for your security team.
- At-rest encryption: all persisted model artifacts, logs, and customer data are AES-256 encrypted.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): we support CMEK via cloud KMS and an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. Need to confirm which you prefer for prod.
- Audit & access logging: logs are available (API call audit, admin changes). You mentioned a 13-month retention target — we can scope retention/ingest/export costs.
- PII retention/erasure: we can configure per-tenant retention windows and have deletion workflows; want to understand your retention policy exactly (regulatory hold windows, e-discovery needs).

Attachments: demo-deck.pdf (attached).

Next steps I propose:
1) We share a short tech-note describing the BYOK/HSM options and implications for key custody and rotation.
2) Aditya to propose how logs/audit exports can be scoped for 13 months and sample log formats.
3) Schedule a 60-min security workshop next week with your InfoSec to validate artifacts (SOC2, pen test summary).

Could you confirm which keys option you prefer (Redwood-managed CMEK, Cloud KMS BYOK, or HSM-backed BYOK) and any mandatory retention/regulatory constraints?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Samar Gupta <samar.gupta@finpay.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: crypto, residency & logging clarifications

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Residency: production must be US-only (primary + backups in-us). Disaster recovery outside US is acceptable only with explicit encryption and legal review.
- Keys: for production we require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 equivalent or cloud provider HSM with audited attestation). For PoC, cloud KMS BYOK is fine.
- TLS: mutual TLS is required for any management/control plane operations that issue credentials.
- Retention: 13 months for audit logs is our baseline for operations; for PII we need variable retention windows by data type (we'll provide a table).
- Evidence: send SOC2 Type II report excerpt and recent pen test summary. Also send a short runbook for key rotation and compromise procedures.

Attaching our security appendix with some of the questions filled out — hope that speeds the review: FinPay_Security_Appendix.docx

Elena — can you confirm timing for the security workshop next week?

Best,
Samar
Director, Infrastructure Security — FinPay

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samar Gupta <samar.gupta@finpay.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: crypto, residency & logging clarifications

Samar — quick technical notes to address the items you raised:

1) HSM-backed keys: Redwood Private supports HSM integrations (customer brings HSM or we orchestrate using cloud HSM modules). For cloud HSM we can provide attestation artifacts and CA chains; for on-prem HSM we can support PKCS#11-based key references.

2) BYOK implications:
   - If you hold keys externally, Redwood will store only key references and never persist cleartext keys. Tokenization and envelope encryption are used for payloads where needed.
   - Key rotation: we support rolling rotation with zero-downtime when using envelope keys; for HSM workflows, rotation requires coordination and a short maintenance window for rewrapping persisted objects.

3) Logs & retention: API audit logs (who/what/when), admin console changes, and request metadata are all exportable via S3-compatible buckets. We can set lifecycle rules to retain 13 months and export compressed archives for long-term storage. Typical export includes timestamp, request id, user, operation, model id, and tenant id.

4) In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with optional mTLS for management endpoints; data plane use of TLS with forward secrecy.

Action needed from FinPay: a short list of compliance drivers (e.g., GLBA, NYDFS, PCI scope decisions) and whether FinPay requires customer-hosted HSM hardware vs cloud HSM attestation. Once we have that, we'll prepare a 2-page technical note and a sample runbook with rotation steps and an S3 export example.

- Aditya
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Korsakov <ekorsakov@finpay.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 10:22:00 +0300
Subject: Re: Post-demo: crypto, residency & logging clarifications

Thanks — a few specifics from our security review:

- HSM requirement: production must use an HSM-backed key store. Cloud HSM with attestation is acceptable if you can supply the attestation report and the KMS provider cert.
- Rotation: rotation cadence targeted at 90 days for wrapping keys; need a documented rollback plan and test steps.
- PII: we will provide the table of retention windows by data classification by Monday.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II excerpt + the latest pen test executive summary are high priority. Please also include TLS cipher suites supported and whether you support only TLS 1.3 for data plane (we prefer 1.3 where possible).

Can you confirm a workshop on Tue (23 Jul) 09:30 PT? We'll have our lead cryptographer and infra lead join.

Elena
Head of Infrastructure Security — FinPay
